name: State Museum of Arts of the Republic of Karakalpakstan (Savitsky Museum)
funding: State museum with about 70,000 visitors in 2025; the government-backed ACDF paid for its renovation, restorers and digitisation.
watch: Savitsky's collection of banned Soviet avant-garde art; refurbished by the state ACDF.
records_note: The museum site has no annual reports, accounts or funder list; it names the director and a deputy for finance but no board.

name: State Museum of Arts of Uzbekistan
funding: A state museum founded in 1918 with over 100,000 objects; a new Tadao Ando building is commissioned by the state ACDF, broke ground 27 Aug 2025 and is due in Mar 2028.
watch: Its rebuild is run by the same state foundation as the Bukhara Biennial, whose lead partners include Bukhara Oil.
records_note: The museum and its renovation sponsor, the Art and Culture Development Foundation, publish no reports, accounts or funder list, and name only a chairperson.

name: State of Concept Athens
funding: European Cultural Foundation, Outset Contemporary Art Fund, Greek Ministry of Culture; non-profit foundation.
watch: First non-profit contemporary art institution in Athens, founded by iLiana Fokianaki; focused on geopolitical, environmental, and feminist inquiry.

name: Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam
funding: €37.5M income (2024), City of Amsterdam 62%. VriendenLoterij is main partner; IMC, ABN AMRO, Mastercard, Polestar and Teijin are loyal partners; Ammodo and the Mondriaan Fund also give.
watch: ABN AMRO is a loyal partner (2024 report). It paid €480M in 2021 to settle a Dutch money-laundering case covering 2014 to 2020.
records_note: The Stedelijk's 2024 report summary, on its own file host, names partners and gives a financial overview with an auditor's opinion; its website blocked checks.

name: Stiftung Stadtmuseum Berlin
funding: Senatsverwaltung für Kultur und Gesellschaftlichen Zusammenhalt Berlin funding across Märkisches Museum, Nikolaikirche, and Ephraim-Palais.

name: STPI Creative Workshop & Gallery
funding: Non-profit founded 2002; National Arts Council support plus patrons (S$2,500 individual, S$5,000 corporate) targeting S$300k.
watch: No named patrons are published. No controversy found.
records_note: Its About page names ten board members; it posts no annual reports, accounts or funder list, and the governance page is one paragraph.

name: Studio Voltaire
funding: Arts Council England core funding; Mayor of London; trusts including Wolfson, Garfield Weston, Foyle and Henry Moore Foundation; corporate patrons BakerMcKenzie and Fletcher Gallery Services; a Council of supporters.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies supported its website through the Digital Accelerator Programme. 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop Bloomberg in May 2026.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the supporters and funders page names funders undated, and trustees are listed.

name: Tabakalera (International Centre for Contemporary Culture)
funding: Public centre funded by Gipuzkoa council, San Sebastián city and the Basque government.
watch: Former tobacco factory; no current tobacco funding found.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2020 to 2025 with income and spending tables, a 2024 budget and its named board, but no funder list.

name: Taipei Contemporary Art Center
funding: Artist-run space founded 2010. In 2013 its director said most money came from sales of donated artworks, plus a small government subsidy (about 15%). No current funder list found.
watch: JUT Land Development gave the building 2009 to 2012. The centre's own site fails its certificate check; no 2025 or 2026 programme found.
records_note: Its website returns only an error page (live and in an August 2026 archive copy), so nothing could be checked.

name: Taiwan Contemporary Culture Lab (C-LAB)
funding: State: run since 2018 by the Ministry of Culture's Taiwan Living Arts Foundation; budget figure not found.
watch: State-funded lab; the funder is the Ministry of Culture via its foundation. The only criticism found is a gentrification complaint.
records_note: Its operator, Taiwan Living Arts Foundation, posts annual reports 2018 to 2025, financial statements, a donations and subsidies list and its trustees.

name: Talbot Rice Gallery
funding: University of Edinburgh gallery; 2025-26 shows credit ECA, Creative Scotland, Henry Moore Fdn, British Council, MGS, Polish culture ministry.
watch: Wael Shawky show (2025) co-funded by the Alwaleed Centre, endowed by Saudi Prince Alwaleed bin Talal.
records_note: The gallery publishes nothing itself; the University of Edinburgh posts annual reports, accounts and its Court; the gallery names funders only on exhibition pages.

name: Tallinn Art Hall (Tallinna Kunstihoone)
funding: Cultural Endowment of Estonia (Eesti Kultuurkapital), Ministry of Culture of Estonia; public non-profit art institution.
watch: Functionalist kunsthalle on Freedom Square, built in 1934; its exhibitions address contemporary democracy.
